question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

I saw so much of those peasant carts in your yard.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the phrase "**so much**" instead of "**so many**."
 
• "Carts" is a plural countable noun and should be paired with "many" instead of "much."
 
• The correct phrase should be "**so many**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I saw **so many of those** peasant carts in your yard."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "of those peasant"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 2: "No error"** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in Option 3.
 
• **Option 4: "carts in your yard."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
